messages:
sara_support: FYI just escalated a customer billing dispute. They claim they were charged for a partial SSE response after a hotspot toggle. Attaching logs and repro notes below. Can someone triage?

mike_oncall: Thanks — can you paste the client-side repro and any request IDs / trace IDs?

sara_support: From customer: 'iPhone 15, iOS 17.2. App uses SSE / EventSource. While streaming, user toggled Personal Hotspot on -> off -> on. Stream abruptly ended with a partial JSON chunk: `{'choices': [{'text': "...some text cut of"` and client reported 502 on reconnect. They logged request-id header: `x-req-id: rwd-9f2a3b` and trace: `trace-id=tr-7c1`

sara_support: Client-side repro steps they provided:
1) Start SSE connect to `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat` (token scoped).
2) Let stream produce ~120 tokens.
3) Turn on Personal Hotspot (phone becomes AP), quick toggle back to carrier, waits ~3s
4) App sees `EventSource.onerror` then connection close. Reconnect returns `502 Bad Gateway` then succeeds but last event was truncated.

sara_support: Customer included server snippet of last chunk: 
```
data: {"id":"msg_123","object":"chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"We recommend updating your con"},"finish_reason":null}]}

# then stream closed abruptly
```

ben_runtime: That looks like partial token emission + TCP reset during transport. Do we have proxy / LB logs for rwd-9f2a3b?

triage-bot: pull-logs rwd-9f2a3b -> job 48211 queued (ETA ~20s)

mike_oncall: Two quick asks: (1) did the client send `Connection: keep-alive` + proper `Accept: text/event-stream`? (2) any SSL/TLS renegotiation logs from customers network?

sara_support: Customer supplied request headers excerpt: 
```
GET /v1/streams/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
Connection: keep-alive
User-Agent: AcmeMobile/4.2 iOS/17.2
x-req-id: rwd-9f2a3b
```

ben_runtime: Good. We're likely seeing a midflight TCP FIN/RST from the device during NAT rebinding. That can cut the socket while our runtime is mid-chunk write leading to truncated event. We should check: (a) if our edge retries or returns partial 200+EOF vs 502, (b) if we are flushing chunk boundaries atomically.

triage-bot: logs pulled: job 48211 -> attached 6 log segments (available at https://internal.redwood/logs/rwd-9f2a3b)

mike_oncall: Opening the logs now. Observed sequence: connection accepted -> stream open -> continuous token writes -> at T+12.34s we see upstream error: `upstream prematurely closed connection (connection reset by peer)` -> LB returns 502 to client on the followup reconnect attempt.

mike_oncall: So cause: client-side network reset. Impact: our runtime wrote N bytes, kernel accepted but peer closed before full write confirmed. We emitted partial SSE event.

alexa_billing: The billing team says the customer was charged for the partial output. They want options: prorate, refund, or credit. We need customer-facing language: does the platform consider a stream with truncated final event as 'successful usage'?

ben_runtime: Internally token accounting logs show tokens counted up to last emitted token; billing pipeline doesn't currently differentiate aborted vs completed streams.

mike_oncall: Short-term mitigation options: (a) detect abrupt upstream close mid-event and mark the session as "aborted" but we've already counted tokens — we'd need a billing correction. (b) implement idempotent-event markers and server-side buffering so that events are only acknowledged/charged on full-event flush (longer term).

sara_support: Customer wants a refund. Suggested reply: explain network cause, offer one-time credit and escalate to billing for refund. Also ask for network capture from device (pcap) if they want deeper investigation.

alexa_billing: I'll approve a one-time credit for the disputed invoice and flag billing rule for review. Please provide the request id and invoice.

ben_runtime: For engineering follow-up, I'll file an intern ticket: "sse: ensure atomic event emission or mark partial writes and expose abort reason in usage logs". Also propose a tiny change: add an SSE footer event `event: _complete\ndata: {"status":"ok"}\n` at stream end for completed responses. If footer missing and socket closed, we mark as aborted.

mike_oncall: Agree. Also add enhanced edge logging: if we receive `RST`/`FIN` during write, log byte offset and last-complete-event-id. Will help future disputes.

sara_support: Reply text for customer (short): "Thanks — looks like the disconnect happened due to the device network switching mid-stream which caused a truncated event. We've issued a one-time credit while we investigate hardening the stream semantics. Could you share the invoice number and, if possible, a packet capture or reproducible short video of the toggle?"

sara_support: tagging @alexa_billing for action and @ben_runtime to file the internal engineering ticket. :thumbsup:

ben_runtime: Filing ticket now -> TKT-7791. Will add proposed footer + edge logging prototype.

mike_oncall: If anyone can grab a quick repro on android as well that would be helpful — different TCP stacks behave differently.

sara_support: I'll follow up with customer and paste invoice + pcap if they provide it. Closing thread for now, will reopen if more info comes in. :v:
